clue.text: Charge made by man at the embassy

parts.note: Al is a short man's name, standing for any man
a legation is a diplomatic mission, a lesser embassy

explanation.surface: An accusation is levelled by someone working at a foreign embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation, especially one not yet proved, is a formal assertion of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Primate seen around Sabbath in church

indicators.note: the word for a primate is placed around the letter for Sabbath, enclosing it

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is spotted wandering around a church on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link word; the definition 'in church' points to a part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is found inside the building.

clue.text: He won't look you in the eye when spoken to

definitions.text: He won't look you in the eye when spoken to

parts.words: He won't look you in the eye when spoken to
parts.note: reads as a shifty, evasive person, but describes someone who watches the speaker's mouth to follow speech

explanation.surface: A rude or shifty man avoids eye contact in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person following speech by watching lip movements looks at the mouth rather than the eyes.

explanation.surface: Allocate a prize at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or bestow is one sense; a sum of money given to a student or researcher is the other.

clue.text: A classic feature of English woods?

definitions.text: A classic feature of English woods?

parts.words: A classic feature of English woods?
parts.note: reads as typical woodland trees, but a 'classic' is one of the five big English flat horse races, run at Epsom

explanation.surface: The trees most typical of an English forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Classics are five major flat horse races; this one, for fillies, is run at Epsom racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The fillies' race at Epsom is one of the five Classics, and the trees named are typical of English woodland.

indicators.note: distilling transforms a substance, so the letters of the drug's name are reworked

explanation.surface: A drug is extracted by distillation from seawater.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marine belongs to or comes from the great expanse of salt water.

clue.text: At short notice, sent back information

indicators.note: sending back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an ad is a short form of advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: Someone returned the details at very short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns ATAD, giving the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for reference or analysis are information.

parts.note: reads as a measure of berries, but describes the oak's nut sitting in its little cup

explanation.surface: A cup filled with berries or fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is a fruit held in a scaly cup-shaped base.

parts.note: suggests someone from a small Polynesian island, but the island is a whole continent in the Pacific region

explanation.surface: Someone who lives on an island in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the island continent bordered by the Pacific could be called a Pacific islander.

parts.note: reads as a royal command to attend the palace, and also a legal order to attend a law court

explanation.surface: Ordered to attend the royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called by official order to attend, such as a witness to a trial, is this.

clue.text: Returned copies include one in colour

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the numeral inside it, enclosing it
returned means the word for copiers is read backwards

parts.note: apes as a verb means copies or imitates
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Copies sent back include one printed in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns APES into SEPA, and 'include' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown shade, familiar from old photographs, is a colour.

clue.text: They have the will to settle things

definitions.text: They have the will to settle things

parts.words: They have the will to settle things
parts.note: reads as determined people, but the will is a testament they carry out after a death

explanation.surface: Determined people who are resolved to sort matters out.
explanation.definitionFit: People appointed to carry out a dead person's testament hold the document and settle the estate.

clue.text: Stop and relax with a shower

parts.note: to rest is to relax
a shower is a short spell of rain

explanation.surface: Halt and unwind under a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or check something is to stop it.

indicators.note: half signals the first half of the word minute is taken

explanation.surface: Thirty seconds or under.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser or smaller in amount or importance is a synonym.

parts.note: a sleeping partner is a silent investor in business, but here it is literally those who share a bed, figuratively allies

explanation.surface: Investors who take no active part in a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally those who share a bed, figuratively close associates or allies.

clue.text: Makes beloved listeners follow the final point

indicators.note: follow means the word for listeners is placed after the word for the final point

parts.note: the end is the final point
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: An audience follows a speech to its last point and grows fond.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause someone to be loved or held dear is the sense.

indicators.note: wayward means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strays in the middle of a crowd of wayward sweethearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans or suitors who are keen on someone are their lovers.

clue.text: Business needs a new angle in the freeze

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: new signals the word angle is made over in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A firm facing a pay freeze must find a fresh approach.
explanation.definitionFit: To set or solidify, especially through cold, is to freeze.

parts.note: a resigned shrug at fate, read literally as a definition of being alive

explanation.surface: A resigned exclamation at bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive and living is the state the exclamation literally names.

parts.note: reads as an advantage, but a hand is a worker, and the upper one is the boss of the workers

explanation.surface: Being in a position of advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker; the one in charge of a group of workers is the senior hand.

clue.text: Writer comes up with a melody for a god

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for a writer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: An author arrives with a song for a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of the sea is a god.

parts.note: made, as in 'made to do it', means forced

indicators.note: out signals the letters of air are disordered

explanation.surface: Air pushed out of a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from a Portuguese Atlantic island is an example.

explanation.surface: Teachers taking part in an American golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmasters are teachers; the Augusta event each April is a famous American golf major.

indicators.note: formation signals the letters are formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Change the line-up of a team, but not just now.
explanation.definitionFit: At a subsequent time, rather than now, means not yet.

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to be captured on film.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up with sticky strip is one sense; captured on a cassette or video is the other.

clue.text: One way to check payment by cheque?

definitions.text: One way to check payment by cheque?

parts.words: One way to check payment by cheque?
parts.note: check here means delay, putting a later day on the cheque so it cannot be cashed yet

explanation.surface: A method of verifying a payment made by cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a future day on a cheque holds back, or checks, when it can be paid.

parts.note: suggests drugged lovers, but the fruit of the palm has its stones removed

explanation.surface: Romantic partners might be high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic escorts are one sense; the palm fruit, often sold with stones removed, is the other.

parts.note: reads as an execution, but describes a sliding bar shot across a door to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone executed on grounds of national security.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal bar slid, or shot, across a door fastens it securely.

clue.text: After work, quiet or music is timely

indicators.note: after work means the following letters come once the work is in place

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: After a day's work, silence or a song is welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming at a convenient or well-chosen moment is a synonym for timely.

clue.text: It takes two to add zest to love

parts.note: tang is a sharp zesty flavour
O, the zero score in tennis, is love

explanation.surface: Two people are needed to spice up a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'it takes two to tango', a dance for a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American dance performed by a couple needs two people.

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the word residence

explanation.surface: A squad lives together in shared accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports team, such as an eleven, is a side.

clue.text: Prettiness in a constantly recurring form

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new form means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Beauty that keeps coming back in a repeated shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting or returning continually is what persisting, relentless things do.
